key_insight: MedJev delivers competitive zero-shot medical predictions locally on a laptop, but patient-level confidence estimates require recalibration.
clinical_relevance: Low computational demands could support local clinical decision-support research, though benchmark performance does not establish clinical safety or benefit.
method: Answers structured questions in one forward pass without generating text.
Evaluated across 10 medical benchmarks against zero-shot LLMs, published GPT results, and supervised models.
Uses two-parameter recalibration with 50–200 labeled local examples.
evidence_signal: MedJev achieved 72.5% MedQA accuracy and 0.926 in-hospital mortality AUROC on MIMIC-based evaluation; reported recalibration reduced patient-level expected calibration error from 0.286 to 0.007.
watch_item: Strong mortality discrimination did not generalize to all tasks: ED admission AUROC trailed a supervised comparator (0.745 vs. 0.809), and uncalibrated patient-level confidence was unreliable.
paper_title: MedJev: Evaluating Zero-Shot System-One Decision Making in Medicine
